parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence since 1978, no documented police, border or violence targeting, and documented historically tolerant attitudes with visible LGBTQ scene and Pride since 2017. Resident surgery requirement for gender recognition, 2015 employment ban and federal hate-crime coverage are climate signals only for a visitor using home documents; no documented traveler-facing facility, border-document or care protection is shown operating, and no trans-specific violence or enforcement data exists. Military ban applies to stationed personnel, not civilian visitors. This sits a step below acceptance-with-working-protections, above friction-only regimes.

street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of trans-specific data in thin record is not evidence of safety; social acceptance may reduce street friction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: formal protections exist with occasional friction and working remedies. This case has no documented incident or remedy, and less documented traveler-facing protection, so not higher; no detention or hostility similar to its safe capital experience keeps it near this level.

Lower: 0.75-C documents border acceptance of matching markers, training, tribunal appeal and compensation. This dossier documents none of those traveler-facing operating protections, only resident law and general tolerance, so it cannot reach that tier.

Materially lower: 0.85-A has explicit equality law, self-ID documents, independent oversight and documented discipline/compensation. Here surgery-based recognition, no documented enforcement and no trans-specific data leave substantial unknowns, well below 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: island and federal layers interact without documented traveler-facing hostility. Law is permissive on sexuality and marriage, society is described as tolerant with historically accepting culture, and no trans-specific targeting is documented, limiting severity if outed. Counterweights are structural unknowns: resident surgery requirement, federal military ban for stationed personnel, and absence of documented operative traveler protections or trans-specific violence/police data. Hence reduced but not low risk, a step below documented acceptance-plus-protections.
